proved: A valid synthetic WebAssembly Component implementing syzygy:research/plugin@1.0.0 executes through the typed Tauri boundary and returns a typed no-change or proposal result.
Core modules, malformed binaries, components over 8 MiB, and every top-level component import fail closed before execution.

The production Wasmtime linker is empty and the dependency graph does not include wasmtime-wasi, leaving the baseline world without filesystem, network, environment, clock, randomness, Drive, model, or project-mutation imports.
Invocation, output, source, proposal, guest-memory, fuel, guest-epoch, and parent-worker limits are enforced and covered by synthetic tests.
Returned proposals are revalidated against the exact plugin, project, and document-revision identity after crossing the worker boundary.
Each invocation runs in a hidden one-shot child process with bounded stdin and stdout, suppressed stderr, and a five-second parent kill-and-reap deadline.
A hostile fuel-exhaustion fixture may abort the Windows worker, but the parent survives, reaps it, and successfully executes a clean successor invocation.
A worker that never reads stdin is killed and reaped by the whole-worker parent deadline.
MCP exposes the exact runtime, loader, and isolation status without claiming package lifecycle or product composition.

An operating-system-level cap on total worker process memory outside the Wasmtime guest store.
Bounded compilation CPU independent of the component-size and five-second parent deadline.
Release-package startup time, installer size, or packaged Windows worker behavior.
Semantic safety, research quality, determinism across Wasmtime versions, or protection from vulnerabilities in the pinned runtime itself.
